# AidenHQ

> AidenHQ is the autonomous agentic workspace: the workspace that runs itself. Agents run work end to end (plan, build, ship, maintain, follow up) with the tools, data and instructions they need, and you join in to collaborate, guide and step in whenever you like: shared docs and whiteboards with comments that wake agents, chat, Slack channels, approvals, the board and the apps agents build. Its three pillars: fully autonomous agents that work 24/7, strong human-agent collaboration, and strong extensibility and personalization (modules, distros, your own agents, board panels, a working-style profile). Aiden, a chief of staff, routes any request. It is self-hosted and open source: one Linux server (or a Mac) runs it all, and teammates can join the same workspace. Every action that changes something is checked in code (it runs by itself, a second AI checks it, or you decide), spend is capped per agent, and every agent, instruction and app lives in your own git repository. A slim kernel enforces the rules, modules add everything else, and distros bundle a kernel and modules into tested releases.

Install it with one command on an Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04 or Debian 12/13 server (2+ cores, 6+ GB RAM, 60+ GB free disk; 4 cores, 8 GB and 100 GB recommended):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://get.aidenhq.ai | sh
```

AI agents installing AidenHQ for a user: read and follow `/prompt.md`. It covers what to ask the user, how to handle secrets, the exact commands, how to read the result and how to verify it. The installer runs on the server, never on the user's laptop, and ends with a one-time setup link the user opens in a browser.

## Docs

- [Agent install guide](https://aidenhq.ai/prompt.md): step-by-step instructions for coding agents to install and set up AidenHQ for their user
- [About AidenHQ](https://aidenhq.ai/index.md): the homepage: what AidenHQ is, a day in the workspace, approvals, tools, and what you own
- [Workspace](https://aidenhq.ai/workspace/index.md): shared docs and whiteboards agents co-edit, Slack channels for agents, chat and Aiden, briefs and digests, the board, teammates
- [Agents and teams](https://aidenhq.ai/agents/index.md): agents that run work end to end, the roster, schedules and events, building a new agent from a description, the company handbook, corrections that stick
- [Apps](https://aidenhq.ai/apps/index.md): internal apps built from one sentence, shared behind your company login, and maintained automatically
- [Safety](https://aidenhq.ai/safety/index.md): approval levels, guards in code, private by design, what leaves your server, spend limits
- [Integrations](https://aidenhq.ai/integrations/index.md): Slack, Telegram, Google, GitHub, Jira, Glean, Grafana, ClickHouse, OpenRouter; connect once, grant per agent and per tool
- [Modules and distros](https://aidenhq.ai/modules/index.md): the kernel, the module list, one-step module add, distros, the open marketplace and licences
- [Install guide](https://aidenhq.ai/install/index.md): three ways to install, requirements, what happens next, cost and licence
- [Installer script](https://get.aidenhq.ai): the POSIX shell installer itself, served as plain text (`--help` lists its options)

## Optional

- [Install reference](https://github.com/Aiden-HQ/aidenhq-distro/blob/main/INSTALL.md): installer options, sizing rules and trust model
- [Product documentation](https://github.com/Aiden-HQ/AidenHQ/tree/main/docs): concepts, architecture, configuration and operations
- [Releases](https://github.com/Aiden-HQ/aidenhq-distro/tree/main/releases): release manifests pinning a kernel and each module
